clue.text: Man possibly getting little cash in retirement

annotationWithheld.why: Man possibly getting little cash in retirement (5): BED (retirement) round P (little cash) gives only BPED; no clue word accounts for the I, and the scan prints the clue the same
annotationWithheld.clue: Man possibly getting little cash in retirement

clue.text: Delivery secures wicket before end of the game

indicators.note: the delivery word holds the wicket within it

parts.note: a ball is a delivery in cricket
a wicket is a small gate

indicators.note: the last letter of the word the is taken

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler takes a wicket just before the match ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' takes E from 'the'; 'wicket' here is a small gate, not the cricket stumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagatelle is a table game in which balls are struck into numbered holes.

clue.text: Lots of people in church, say, bringing flowers

indicators.note: say shows that the word is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a congregation is a minister's flock, so several are flocks

explanation.surface: Churchgoers bring flowers to decorate the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlox are garden plants with clusters of bright blooms.

clue.text: Foolish official has to follow through, admitting blunder

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely

indicators.note: the word for through lets the blunder in

parts.note: by can mean through, as in by means of
to err is to blunder

explanation.surface: An incompetent bureaucrat has to see a task through and owns up to a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: Dogberry is the bumbling constable in Shakespeare's Much Ado About Nothing; 'follow' is a verb here, to dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogberry is the self-important, blundering constable in a Shakespeare comedy, the model of a foolish official.

clue.text: Justification for holding monarch in respect

indicators.note: the justification word grips the monarch's letters in its middle, as something held

parts.note: a defence is a justification offered for what one did
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone explains why they kept the king in high esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing deference means showing polite regard, the same as respect.

clue.text: Many a tear in intermittent flow

definitions.meaning: a tear falling from the eye is a single drop
a leak that comes drop by drop rather than in a stream

explanation.definitionFit: A drip is a single falling drop, and also the slow drop-by-drop leaking of a liquid.

clue.text: General fighting without making any charges

definitions.meaning: a brawl in which everyone joins in
open to everyone at no cost

explanation.definitionFit: A free-for-all is a disorderly brawl involving everyone; literally it means available at no charge to anyone.

clue.text: Take another look at this publication

definitions.meaning: a magazine or journal of criticism, often titled as such

explanation.definitionFit: To review is to reconsider; a review is also a periodical publishing critical articles.

clue.text: I get tea on free treat

indicators.note: the letters are set free to fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is offered tea as a free treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treat' is the verb, to treat with someone, i.e. bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat with someone is to discuss terms, which is to bargain or parley.

clue.text: People editor's brought in to make corrections

indicators.note: the people are brought into the editor's abbreviation

parts.note: ED is the usual abbreviation for editor
men are people

explanation.surface: Staff are hired by an editor to correct copy.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to revise it by correcting errors.

clue.text: Withdraw pin to fire explosive

indicators.note: to withdraw is to draw back, so the word for pin is read backwards

parts.note: pins is slang for legs, so a pin is a leg
to fire something is to set it alight, ignite it

explanation.surface: Instructions for setting off a grenade: pull the pin to detonate the explosive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pin' looks like the grenade's firing pin, but pins is slang for legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelignite is a blasting explosive made from nitroglycerine, so it is an example of an explosive.

clue.text: Nothing, for a change, in vague fashion

indicators.note: something is swapped out of the word vague, the zero going in instead of a letter

parts.note: O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone's vague dress sense might be improved by nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' swaps the A of VAGUE for O.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in vogue is in fashion; vogue means the prevailing style.

clue.text: Try to get pieces for collectors

parts.note: to tax someone is to try their patience
chess pieces are called men

explanation.surface: Someone tries to get a share of the takings for the collectors.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxmen are tax collectors, the officials who gather revenue.

clue.text: Played very loud note inside camp

indicators.note: the loud mark and the note sit inside the word for played

parts.note: an actor who played a part acted it
FF is fortissimo, very loud in music
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A musician blares a note at a holiday camp concert.
explanation.definitionFit: Camp behaviour is exaggerated and showy, much like affected manners.

clue.text: Struggled to hold on to note when financially embarrassed

indicators.note: the struggle word grips the note inside itself

parts.note: strained means made a great effort, struggled
TE is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A singer battled to sustain a note while short of money.
explanation.definitionFit: In straitened circumstances means short of money, which is being financially embarrassed.

clue.text: Research centre provided by non-U party and an opponent

indicators.note: non-U says the letter U is to be left out of the party's name

parts.note: Labour is a British political party
an gives the letter A
a Tory is a Conservative, the traditional opponent of Labour in Britain

explanation.surface: A think tank is funded by a party and its opponent together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-U' drops U from LABOUR to give the American spelling LABOR; 'non-U' also puns on the old idea of upper-class (U) speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A laboratory is a place where scientific research is carried out.

clue.text: Gambler departing in profit

parts.note: a better is one who bets, a gambler
off means leaving, as in 'I'm off'

explanation.surface: A punter leaves the course with winnings.
explanation.definitionFit: Being better off means having more money than before, i.e. ahead financially.

clue.text: Damage resulting from hydrogen weapon

parts.note: H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: The destruction caused by a hydrogen bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm and damage are synonyms, both meaning injury or loss.

clue.text: Outdated as a fairy cake might be?

definitions.meaning: old and shabby, past its best

definitions.text: as a fairy cake might be?
definitions.meaning: a cake for fairies might be one nibbled by winged insects that resemble them

explanation.definitionFit: Moth-eaten means worn and antiquated; literally it describes cloth eaten by moths.

clue.text: Wild parties involving a problem for host

indicators.note: wild parties: the letters run riot into another order

explanation.surface: Raucous parties cause trouble for whoever is hosting them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'host' is the animal or plant a parasite lives on, not a party host.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite lives off another organism, its host, and harms it.

clue.text: Artist a very rich collector initially rejected

indicators.note: the first letter of the collector's name is thrown out

parts.note: J. Paul Getty was a famously rich art collector

explanation.surface: A painter's work is turned down by a wealthy collector at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially rejected' drops the G from GETTY.
explanation.definitionFit: William Etty was an English painter, famous for his nudes.

clue.text: Houses in' which older relative accommodates Irishman

indicators.note: the relative's word takes the Irishman in, as a host would

parts.note: a parent is a relative of an older generation
Liam is a typically Irish man's name

explanation.surface: A family where a parent takes in an Irish lodger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Houses' looks like a verb, but it is the definition: the two Houses (Commons and Lords).
explanation.definitionFit: Parliament consists of two Houses, the Commons and the Lords.

clue.text: Is such music kept within bounds by baton always?

definitions.text: Is such music kept within bounds by baton always?

indicators.note: the letters are held inside the words baton always, between their outer letters

explanation.surface: A conductor wonders whether music is always kept in check by the baton.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is tucked inside 'baton always'; the whole clue doubles as a sly question, since such music lacks a key.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonal music has no key centre, so it is not bound by tonality.

clue.text: Watch with interest risky venture by gallery

parts.note: a spec is a speculation, a risky venture
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: Someone eyes a speculative purchase at an art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To spectate is to be an onlooker, someone who watches an event.

clue.text: Fish set out on ice

definitions.meaning: a flat sea fish related to the ray
to glide off over ice on blades

explanation.definitionFit: A skate is a ray-like fish; to skate is to glide on ice in skates.

clue.text: Cover produced by fellow binding books

indicators.note: the fellow's word wraps round the books, like a binding

parts.note: a fellow is a male
NT is the New Testament, books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A bookbinder produces a cover for a volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantle is a cloak, something that covers, or as a verb to cover.

clue.text: Scottish river — the excessively pretty Dee?

parts.note: twee means overly dainty or quaint
Dee is how the letter D is spelt out

explanation.surface: A sentimental description of the River Dee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dee' is a real Scottish river, a decoy; here it is the name of the letter D.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tweed is a river in the Scottish Borders.

clue.text: Old silver used before notes

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
E is a musical note
D is a musical note

explanation.surface: Antique silver used before banknotes came in.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged means elderly or having lived long, so old.

clue.text: A celebration with sailors on deck

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
RN is the Royal Navy, the sailors

explanation.surface: A party is held with sailors on the ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' is the verb meaning decorate, not the ship's floor.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck something is to decorate it, to adorn it.

clue.text: Careless Nigel upset another bloke

indicators.note: Nigel is upset, so his letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, another man

explanation.surface: Nigel is annoyed by another man's carelessness.
explanation.definitionFit: Negligent means failing to take proper care, so careless.

clue.text: Fired along the line, but failed badly in aim

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go in the word for aim

parts.note: an end is a goal or aim, as in ends and means

indicators.note: failed done badly signals a rearrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A sniper fired along the trench but missed the target.
explanation.walkthrough: Enfilade is a military term for fire raking a line from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: Enfilade is gunfire raking a line of troops from end to end, so enfiladed means swept with such fire.

clue.text: Finish bowling, with a side that's short facing one

definitions.text: with a side that's short facing one

parts.note: the end is the finish
a bowler who is bowling is said to be on

explanation.surface: A cricket captain ends a bowler's spell and sets a short fielder facing one batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowling' looks like cricket colour, but a bowler currently bowling is 'on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed end on means positioned with the narrow end pointing towards the viewer.
